Inside the drum are small glass beads, pebbles or clean water, which produce the flowing rustle and the sound of water. The handle is usually wood or rubber, so that the player can shake the body easily. The rim of the frame may have a metal reinforcing ring, adding durability and resonance.

The ocean drum is a percussion instrument of Europe / France, first called the geophone and invented by Olivier Messiaen in 1972 for the orchestral work Des canyons aux étoiles..., taking the idea from Native American water drums. To play, hold it by the frame with the drum face level and roll the wrist so that the body tilts slightly; the metal beads inside roll across the lower face, and different speeds give different sounds, while a sudden start or stop can imitate the sound of waves. It was designed at first to imitate the sound of dry, shifting earth, and later came to be used for images of the sea; it is also used in Buddhist meditation.
海浪鼓的音色具有獨特的流動感與神秘性，音質溫潤而帶有夢幻般的朦朧感。其音域跨度寬: The ocean drum's timbre has a particular flow and mystery, warm and dreamily veiled. Its range is wide, from a deep rumble to a bright high rustle, and it can build a soundscape of many layers. Shaking the glass beads or the water inside makes the drumhead resonate and the sound flow naturally. Compared with the sharp bite of cymbals it is softer and more inward; compared with a shaker it is more penetrating and more dramatic. The instrument can imitate the surging waves of the natural world and give a listening experience that puts you there, which is why it is widely used in contemporary composition and in music therapy.
演奏海浪鼓時，以框架持握，使鼓面保持水平。發聲依靠手腕滾動，讓鼓身朝各方向輕微傾: To play the ocean drum, hold it by the frame and keep the drum face level. The sound comes from rolling the wrist so that the body tilts slightly this way and that, and the metal beads inside roll across the lower face, making a sound like waves on a shore. A beginner can practise slow, even tilts first and learn how different speeds change the sound, then try sudden starts and stops to imitate a breaking wave. The source gives no method book, so practice can only follow the basic order above.
